name: Holo UI Vault — Unified Dual-Dimension Index
description: Style taxonomy, functional classification with 7-dimension Feature Tokens, and harmonization rules. Component paths are in ROUTER.json; token specification in FEATURE_TOKENS.md.

rules: DO NOT read beautifului-components/index.html (32KB human visual preview, wastes tokens).
DO NOT recursively scan directories. Use ROUTER.json for component paths.
Single-task retrieval budget: maximum 1 snippet file + 1 shared CSS file.
Use ROUTER.json for fast path resolution, and FEATURE_TOKENS.md for multi-dimensional disambiguation.
Review STYLE_AND_SELECTION_GUIDE.md prior to combining different styles.

style_harmonization.principle: Beautiful UI provides interaction skeletons; Apple HIG provides visual tokens and physics. They can be seamlessly blended without conflict.
rules: When embedding Beautiful UI components into an Apple-themed project, map container radii to var(--apple-radius-lg) or var(--apple-radius-xl).
Replace dark solid surfaces with Apple Liquid Glass material: background: var(--apple-material-regular); backdrop-filter: var(--apple-blur-regular);
Ensure all clickable elements satisfy the Apple 44pt minimum touch boundary.
Adopt Apple Spring curve: transition-timing-function: var(--apple-ease-spring);
Maintain a single primary style hierarchy per viewport. Do not mix sharp brutalist elements with soft squircles.
Pair Rewamp UI tactile buttons (slide-to-confirm-button, shimmer-button) with Beautiful UI's dense data tables for high-impact action points.
Rewamp UI components use SF Pro and squircle radii, aligning natively with Apple HIG foundations.
When integrating Rewamp UI 3D AI Orbs, contain them in Apple Liquid Glass or Beautiful UI dark cards to maintain visual continuity.
Embed loading.dev micro-indicators (e.g., ld-arc, ld-linear-dots) directly inside Beautiful UI prompt bars and table cells for zero-runtime lightweight feedback without layout shift.
When embedding loading.dev indicators into Apple HIG layouts, set color: var(--apple-accent-blue) or var(--apple-text-secondary) and size to 16px-22px to match SF Pro symbol scales.
Never replace full 3D assistant fluid orbs (Rewamp UI) with micro-spinners; use micro-spinners strictly for atomic operation states.
Embed minimal theme toggles (themetoggle-components) into Beautiful UI or Apple HIG headers with zero CSS conflicts; currentColor automatically adapts to parent typography.
Pair ObsidianUI partner cards (split-showcase) with Apple HIG squircle containers and subtle spring physics for high-fidelity co-marketing showcases.
Pair Arc tactile controls (button, segmented-control, hold-to-confirm) with Beautiful UI or Apple HIG layouts for fluid spring micro-interactions.

items.name: Browser Compat Card

Ships an independently-usable RAMUsageBar. Extends the spirit of CapabilityGate; data source useCapabilities.

items.name: Cache Badge
items.when: Rendering cache badge: Annotates a result as served from the semantic cache, optionally with the hit latency (e.g. "cached · 12ms"). Drive cached/latencyMs from a useSemanticCache lookup result. Renders nothing when cached is false, so it is safe to drop next to any result. Self-contained and presentational.

items.name: Capability Gate
items.when: Rendering capability gate: A true gate: renders its children only when the device meets a stated requirement (e.g. requires="webgpu"), otherwise a themed fallback slot with guidance. The capability check uses useCapabilities. Local models have hard device requirements (LiteRT Gemma is WebGPU-only), so gating prevents a broken experience. The read-only display sibling is DeviceBadge.

items.name: Chrome AI Download Gate
items.when: Rendering chrome ai download gate: The gate a user sees when a Chrome Built-in AI capability exists but its on-device model has not been fetched yet. Chrome refuses to start the model download outside a user activation, so the button is the only way to trigger it. Renders the download prompt, in-flight progress, the failed-attempt message, and the terminal unsupported / cannot-run-here states; returns null once the model is available. Includes ChromeAIReadyBadge. Presentational — bind availability/progress to a provider-fallback hook and pass its download action as onDownload.
items.when_not: Non-React plain HTML pages or heavy monolithic cloud-only backends without browser AI awareness.

items.name: Context Usage Meter
items.when: Rendering context usage meter: A token / context-window budget meter (with composable Context/ContextTrigger/ContextContent/ContextInputUsage/ContextOutputUsage parts) breaking down input/output/reasoning/cache token usage against the model's context-window limit (a hard local GGUF/LiteRT KV-cache constraint), warning near the limit. Fed by usage.tokens from a generate result. Local-only — there is NO cost field. Complements StorageMeter (disk) with a token-budget gauge.
items.when_not: Non-React plain HTML pages or heavy monolithic cloud-only backends without browser AI awareness.

items.name: Device Badge

items.name: Device Capability Grid

Does not replace DeviceBadge.

items.name: Model Downloader

items.name: Model Recommendation Card

items.name: Model Search Browser
items.when: Rendering model search browser: A cmdk-based searchable model-repo browser: a controlled search input, a sort selector (downloads/likes/last-modified), result rows (repo id, author, compact download/like counts, relative last-modified, capped tag badges), load-more pagination, and a per-repo expandable file list (filename, quantization badge, human-readable size) with per-file select actions — plus loading, empty, and error-with-retry states. Purely presentational: every value arrives via props and every action leaves via a callback, so any backend can feed it (recommended wiring: the HuggingFace Hub API; a private registry or static fixtures work identically).

items.name: Model Selector
items.when: Rendering model selector: A device-aware model picker: a list grouped by category, backend filter chips (WebGPU/ONNX/WASM/LiteRT) with live counts, per-model vision/tool-calling/cached badges, a download affordance for uncached models, and a delete-from-cache affordance for cached ones. Device-unfit models (e.g. a WebGPU-only model on a non-WebGPU device) are de-emphasized and labeled. Emits onSelect(modelId) and owns no selection state. Bind models to useModelRecommendations and hasWebGPU to useCapabilities.

items.name: Network Badge
items.when: Rendering network badge: A reactive online/offline indicator (NetworkBadge) sourced from useNetworkStatus, plus an OfflineReady badge that signals the app's required model is cached on-device and can run with no network. Because local models keep working offline, offline is informational, not an error.

items.name: Provider Badge
items.when: Rendering provider badge: Displays the RESOLVED provider identity - composing ProviderFallbackBadge for the tier and name - alongside the model id that actually served the request. While providerName is null it shows a Resolving provider placeholder, so the badge never claims a provider before one has resolved. Takes generic display props (providerName / tier / modelId / note). Distinct from ProviderFallbackBadge (the tier chip it composes): this adds the resolved provider identity plus the served model id. Data source: a provider-fallback resolver.
